headline: Nokia's chief executive says AI data centers would be built twice as fast if shortages of memory chips and power eased.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a fresh interview with a named industry chief, but it is opinion and he gave no figures.
importance_line: It suggests the pace of the AI buildout is held back by chips and power rather than by demand, which matters to utilities, data center builders and investors weighing the risk of overbuilding, but it is the view of a supplier that sells to the buildout and he gave no figures on the shortages.
summary: CNBC reports, as relayed by Briefs Finance, that Nokia chief executive Justin Hotard said on CNBC's Tech Download podcast that the industry cannot be called overbuilt, because customers would probably build twice as fast if shortages of memory chips and energy eased. Hotard, whose Finnish company sells networking equipment that links the chips inside data centers and connects data centers to one another, added that even with no new leading AI model for three years, deploying today's models could drive large progress.
notes: CNBC is the first reporter; its page returned 403, so the text was read through Briefs Finance, Digital Today and TokenPost, which agree on the quotes. The url is CNBC's own page. The remark is a company chief's opinion, and Nokia sells equipment for the buildout.
